review_type: Independent AI linguistic review, not human expert certification or a proof of impossibility
blinding: Fresh reader received only the two exact Latin strings A/B and fixed no-edit criteria. No native pairs, manuscript identity, original CFG decision or root interpretation supplied. No workspace inspection requested. Returned response retained in structured form below.

A.form_assessment: Most forms admit Latin analyses. Rimo is a rare active counterpart of rimor; datu may be ablative of the noun datus. Do not reject them as nonwords.
partial_phrases: res fili admits a genitive construction
fixo regi admits a dative construction
A.whole_assessment: No convincing complete connected interpretation found. The verbal forms do, fis, rimo and possible infinitives regi, recipi were not connected with defensible complements into a whole statement. Fisu debitu fideli remains unresolved; merely generated supines on -u cannot be used as unrestricted ablatives/adjectives.
A.confidence: High that this review has not established a whole reading; does not exclude every possible poetic context.

B.form_assessment: Many genuine Latin words. Nebo may be future of neo; hebeo means be dull, not have. Ly is an attested scholastic quotation particle, so it is not automatically a nonword.
partial_phrases: me tu sidere feri telo saxo: tu subject, feri imperative, me object, sidere/telo/saxo instrumental ablatives; semantically unusual but syntactically possible
perede me admits an imperative plus object
B.whole_assessment: No convincing whole connected interpretation found. Initial me tu sic might be a repeated beginning; repetition alone is not a disproof. Ego ly nebo and the two isolated u lack a demonstrated connected construction. A quotation or letter-name scenario would require additional evidence, not an invented rescue. Eme and hebeo do not resolve those gaps.
B.confidence: High for distinction between intelligible fragments and no demonstrated complete interpretation; B has stronger local sentence formation.

sources.title: Lewis and Short via Logeion, hebeo

root_limits: Fili is morphologically ambiguous; a partial genitive construction does not identify its referent. No fragment translation becomes a Voynich meaning. Sources are reader-supplied linguistic references, not new manuscript evidence.
